name: Idea validation analyst
why: Picks the riskiest guess in an idea, plans the test, reads the result and calls keep, change or stop, the same loop as the idea validation test skill.

name: Test if your idea can own its market
why: Gives an honest market size and a go, fix or stop call, a quick companion to the market sizing skill.

name: Customer discovery interview planner
why: Lists the guesses in an idea, who to talk to and questions that test them, the first step before any survey.

name: Customer interview question writer
why: Fixes draft interview questions so they ask about real past behaviour, matching the interview guide prompt.

name: Interview fact sorter
why: Separates facts from praise and ideas in interview notes, so findings rest on what people did, not what they said they would do.

name: Customer interview program keeper
why: Tracks buyer patterns across interview rounds and says when to stop, the practical side of interview saturation.

name: Survey answer truth checker
why: Scores how far survey answers can be trusted and flags weak questions, the same checks as the survey design and analysis skill.

name: Say-do gap checker
why: Compares what survey answers claim with what behaviour shows and suggests a behaviour test, useful after any stated-preference survey.

name: Price test keeper
why: Plans one reversible live price test and reads the result, the step that confirms a Van Westendorp or Gabor-Granger range.

name: Buyer identity segment finder
why: Groups buyers from reviews and survey answers and sizes each group, a starting point for the segment map prompt.

name: Competitor white space mapper
why: Builds a grid of where no rival is strong, the gap-finding step of the competitor research skill.

name: Monthly competitor watcher
why: Logs what rivals changed this month and the moves worth answering, the core of the monthly market and competitor watch workflow.

name: Quarterly battle card keeper
why: Refreshes a card for each rival from won and lost deals, turning competitor research into answers the sales team can use.
